$comment: Machine-readable adopter-side configuration. Human-readable twin: docs/PORTING.md. Keep the two in sync — verify_citations.py check 2 reads this file to detect defaults that were never substituted.

$kinds.default: Has a working default. Change it only if your repo already uses a different name.
$kinds.detected: Determined by running a command at install time. Never write a literal for these.
$kinds.required: No sensible default exists. The installer must ask, or the feature degrades visibly.
$kinds.optional: Safe to leave empty. The dependent feature turns itself off rather than failing.

rules_doc.description: The always-loaded rules document for your repo. Every skill cites it.

backlog_file.description: Open and actionable items only. Resolved entries move to archive_file.

archive_file.description: Resolved history with citations. Never read by default.

mistakes_file.description: Process mistakes — how work was done wrongly, not what is broken in the code.

design_docs_dir.description: Where spec saves design documents. A trailing slash is expected. If your path contains a space, keep it quoted everywhere it appears in a shell command.

notes_file_pattern.description: Companion notes file naming. The literal token {tool} is replaced with the component's own name. Use '{tool}/NOTES.md' instead if you prefer notes inside each component's folder.

checklist_section.description: Heading text of the backlog section implement-queue reads as its work queue.

default_branch.description: Your repo's default branch. NEVER hardcode this — 'main' and 'master' are both common and getting it wrong silently targets a branch that does not exist.

detect.note: Preferred. Outputs 'origin/<branch>' — strip the 'origin/' prefix. Fails if the repo has no remote, or if origin/HEAD was never set (common in a clone made with --single-branch); 'git remote set-head origin --auto' fixes the latter.
Fallback. Reports the CURRENTLY checked-out branch, which is only the default branch if that is what happens to be checked out. Confirm with the user rather than assuming.

python_cmd.description: Interpreter used by the hook scripts.

detect.note: Preferred. IMPORTANT: test that it actually RUNS, as shown — do not use 'command -v python3'. On Windows, 'python3' is frequently a Microsoft Store stub that resolves successfully on PATH and then fails on execution, so a resolve-only check picks a broken interpreter and reports success.
Fallback, and the working interpreter on most Windows installs. Same rule: verify execution, not resolution.

test_command.description: How to run your test suite. Cited by the code-reviewer agent so it can re-run tests rather than reasoning about whether they would pass. No default is provided on purpose — a wrong test command produces a review that silently never tests anything. If your repo genuinely has no test suite yet, the installer records this value's source as 'confirmed_none' rather than 'left_empty' — a deliberate, informed answer, distinct from the question simply not being answered yet. code-reviewer must then state plainly in its output that no automated tests were run, rather than either fabricating a command or silently reporting clean with nothing actually checked.

lint_command.description: Linter for .githooks/pre-commit. Invoked from a scratch directory with staged file paths appended, so a bare relative path to a linter binary will not resolve — use $REPO_ROOT, which the hook pre-sets. Empty disables the lint step entirely, which is the shipped default.

flagged_surfaces.description: Specific functions, files, or modules in YOUR codebase with a documented history of subtle bugs. A change that would otherwise be Tier 4 gets the full QA gate if it touches one. Ships empty because this is a property of your code. Grow it reactively: add a place when a subtle bug turns out to be in the same place as a previous subtle bug. Keep it short — a list of twenty escalates everything and therefore escalates nothing.

local_delegate.description: Enables the local-delegate component's free local-model draft before /build spends a turn on an eligible task. Not prompted at install and not embedded via template substitution — the local-delegate runner script reads this key live from your resolved .claude/phase-gate-install/variables.json at call time. Populated shape: {"implement": "<your-model-name>"}. A missing key for a given mode means that mode is off; the shipped empty object means the whole feature is off. Requires a local model runtime (e.g. Ollama) serving an HTTP chat API on localhost:11434 — see the local-delegate component's own README for the full mechanism, prerequisites, and limitations.

available_models.description: Which Claude-mainline models you have access to, ordered weakest-to-strongest. This answers 'the strongest Claude-mainline model' (the last entry) — the question spec Step 3.4's non-Fable fallback and verify Step 2's escalation target actually need, since Fable (itself a Claude model, not a different vendor) is deliberately kept out of this list so those two rules stay independently controllable. It does NOT by itself answer 'the strongest model you have, period' — see fable_available below for that question, used by spec Step 1's Tier-1 design-pass switch.

fable_available.description: Reversed 2026-09-05 (the two-axis SDLC redesign) — this used to be review_model_families, whose rule was 'if only one family is available, skip the review VISIBLY rather than running a same-family pass and calling it cross-model.' That's no longer the rule, and the 'family' framing itself was later found to be false: Fable is a Claude model, not a different vendor. Current rule, tier-conditioned (revised again 2026-09-09 after a uniform Fable-first default collapsed the cost ladder to one rung): for Tier 1, Fable when this flag is true and the draft wasn't itself written on Fable (a Fable-drafted design falls to the strongest available_models entry instead, to avoid a same-model pass at the top of the ladder), otherwise a different Claude-mainline model than the one that drafted (checked against available_models above: sonnet-/haiku-drafted reviews on opus, opus-drafted reviews on sonnet); for Tier 2, a different Claude-mainline model than the one that drafted, with Fable reachable only as an explicit further pass, not automatically. Only when nothing else is reachable at all does either tier fall back to the same model in a fresh context. What buys independence is the fresh context plus a different model than the author, not a different vendor. The heading names the actual reviewing model every time (e.g. '## Design review — Opus, fresh context') and never claims more independence than that pass actually had. Skipping is no longer an option in any case — a same-model pass, correctly labeled, is preferred over silently skipping. Separately, when this flag is true, spec Step 1 treats Fable as outranking every entry in available_models when answering 'the strongest model you have, period' — Fable is genuinely the top of the ladder for that question, unlike its tier-conditioned treatment for reviewer selection above.

subagent_models.description: Default model per bundled subagent. docs-writer is mechanical transcription and runs well on the cheapest tier; code-reviewer needs real reasoning. Override per-call when a specific pass warrants it — a review of code that will run on someone else's machine is worth a stronger, more differentiated model.

update_check_enabled.description: Off-switch for the update-notification SessionStart hook. Not asked about during install (default-kind, per this file's own $kinds rule) — the real opt-in moment is selecting the update-notification component itself at step 2; this is a secondary override for an adopter who wants the component installed but the passive check disabled. Resolved into the plan/receipt's variables[] array exactly like every other variable here — the hook reads its own installed receipt.json for the final value rather than re-reading this source file, so no new adopter-side file/schema is introduced for it.
